dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that seeds a peer_confirmations.json record carrying confirmed_pass/confirmed_at, reopens the store, re-records identical material evidence, and asserts the record is migrated once (fields dropped, _dirty True, file rewritten) with a second identical observation being a no-op (_dirty False).
evidence: Docstring claim: '...the former ``confirmed_pass`` / ``confirmed_at`` per-pass fields, which had no production reader (only tests asserted them)...' and commit message: 'each pre-existing record is rewritten once when first re-observed, dropping the two fields.'

Migration logic newly added: peer_confirmations.py:170-183 `previous = self._records.get(key) or {}` ... `if candidate == previous: return` — where `previous` may contain legacy keys but `candidate` never does.
_load keeps legacy keys verbatim: peer_confirmations.py:121-125 filters only on isinstance(value, dict), so a stored record with confirmed_pass/confirmed_at is loaded intact.

search_files over tests/unit/rebar_reconciler for 'confirmed_pass' returns only assertions of the form `assert "confirmed_pass" not in record` on records created within the same test (backfill:73, snapshot:92,219, store:162,398) — none seed a legacy record with the field then re-observe.

Named violating input: an on-disk record {"source_id":"src-local","target_id":"dst-local","relation":"blocks","link_id":"500","direction":"snapshot","source":"snapshot","confirmed_pass":"pass-1","confirmed_at":123,"first_confirmed_at":100} re-observed with identical material evidence must be rewritten once (dropping the two fields, _dirty True), and a second identical re-observation must be a no-op (_dirty False) — no test drives this.
dropped.finding: The one-time migration of pre-existing on-disk records (rewriting a legacy record once to drop confirmed_pass/confirmed_at, then staying no-op) is asserted by the commit message and record() docstring but is untested. All 'confirmed_pass not in record' assertions verify freshly-created records that never carried the fields; none load a legacy record and confirm it is migrated exactly once.
scenarios: An operator upgrades: peer_confirmations.json already contains records with confirmed_pass/confirmed_at from the prior code; the first reconcile pass after upgrade must migrate them.
A future refactor to the candidate/previous comparison (e.g. normalizing keys) could break the migration silently since no test drives a legacy-shaped previous.
dropped.suggested_fix: Write the store JSON directly with legacy confirmed_pass/confirmed_at fields, open_store, call record()/confirm_from_snapshot with identical material evidence, assert `confirmed_pass`/`confirmed_at` absent and `_dirty is True` after the first re-observe, then assert a second identical re-observe leaves `_dirty is False` and the on-disk bytes unchanged.
